trial_court: 5th Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Saran at Chapra in Sessions Trial No. 100 of 2006
case_name: Dinanath Tiwari & Ors vs The State Of Bihar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Dinanath Tiwari, Kamla Devi, Ravi Kant Tiwari, Hari Bans Tiwari (husband, wife, sons)

facts_of_case: Appellants stand convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A)/34, 304(B)/34 and 201/34 of the Indian Penal Code. They killed Soni Devi, wife of appellant No. 4/Hari Bans Tiwari, for non-fulfilment of dowry demand.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the prosecution to prove its case.
legal_principles.held: Assuming but not admitting that such statement was made six months ago, the case would not fall within the category of dowry death as the deceased cannot be said to have been tortured soon before her death.

legal_principles.principle: The law requires evidence to support the prosecution's version.
legal_principles.held: Evidence, it has been suggested, has come during the course of the trial that there was no telephone in the matrimonial home of the deceased and no letter, intimating such ill-treatment and torture, was ever brought on record.

outcome.final_order: Appellants sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 3 years each for the offences under Sections 498(A)/34 and 201/34, and to pay a fine of Rs. 2,000/- for each of the offences.
